prose.title: The Roman Civil Wars
prose.summary: Two civil wars that can tear the Roman Republic apart, but only when a human plays Rome. In the first, the provinces of five legions break away to the Roman Rebels. In the second, whoever won the first war splits four ways.
prose.breaks_away_from: Rome in the first war; in the second, whichever side won the first
prose.who_it_can_happen_to: Only when a human plays Rome. With a computer-run Rome neither war happens.
what_sets_it_off: First civil war: It is turn 122 (240 BC) or later and Rome holds more than 150 settlements.
First civil war: The Italic revolt has already happened and is over.
First civil war: Rome holds 5 or more regions in each of at least 5 legion recruiting areas.
First civil war: It breaks out at the end of a Roman turn in which a Roman family general is out in the field.
Second civil war: The first war has been decided (the losing side is down to its last settlement) and 2 more turns have passed.
Second civil war: The winner holds more than 200 settlements and 5 or more regions in at least 6 of the 10 legion recruiting areas.
Second civil war: From then on there is a 35% chance at the start of each of the winner's turns. Once it succeeds, the provinces rise 3 turns later.
what_happens: First civil war: A message, 'A Divided Republic', asks whether you stay with Rome (the Populares) or switch to the Roman Rebels (the Optimates). The war happens either way.
First civil war: Rome's settlements in the Germanica, Gallica, Cyrenaica, Parthica and Alaudae legion areas join the Roman Rebels. The other legion areas and the city of Rome stay loyal.
First civil war: The rebel cities are held by strong garrisons of Leves Armaturae and Legionary Cohorts.
First civil war: If you switch sides, the Roman Rebels receive 30000 and you take them over on the next turn, when their leader lands in central Italy.
Second civil war: The winner's largest legion area breaks away to the loser of the first war, the next largest to a second Roman Rebels faction, and the region of Rome itself to The Roman Senate.
Second civil war: All four Roman factions are at war with each other.

Both wars: A beaten Roman faction may offer to surrender to you: a 20% chance each turn once you have taken at least 2 of its settlements and it is down to fewer than 6 (for The Roman Senate, between 6 and 12). Accepting hands you all its settlements.
prose.playing_as_the_rebels: In the first war, the 'A Divided Republic' message lets you switch to the Roman Rebels. In the second, you are offered one after another the loser of the first war, the second Roman Rebels faction and The Roman Senate; turning one down moves on to the next. Turn them all down and you carry on as you were.
